sentences.text: Before coming to the merits of the case, it is necessary to discuss the provision of Section 438 of BNSS (corresponding Section 397 CrPC).

Section 438 of BNSS provides as under:-
"438. Calling for records to exercise powers of revision.

( 1) The High Court or any Sessions Judge may call for and examine the record of any proceeding before any inferior Criminal Court situate within its or his local jurisdiction for the purpose of satisfying itself or himself as to the correctness, legality or propriety of any finding, sentence or order, recorded or passed, and as to the regularity of any proceedings of such inferior Court, and may, when calling, for such record, direct that the execution of any sentence or order be suspended, and if the accused is in confinement that he be released on bail or on his own bond pending the examination of the record.
Explanation.--All Magistrates, whether Executive or Judicial, and whether exercising original or appellate jurisdiction, shall be deemed to be inferior to the Sessions Judge for the purposes of this sub-section and of section 439.
( 2) The powers of revision conferred by sub-section (1) shall not be exercised in relation to any interlocutory order passed in any appeal, inquiry, trial or other proceeding.

(3) If an application under this section has been made by any person either to the High Court or to the Sessions Judge, no further application by the same person shall be entertained by the other of them."
7.

Before proceeding further, the provisions of Section 498A IPC are reproduced as under:
"498A. Husband or relative of husband of a woman subjecting her to cruelty.--

Whoever, being the husband or the relative of the husband of a woman, subjects such woman to cruelty shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years and shall also be liable to fine.
Explanation.--

For the purpose of this section, "cruelty" means-- (a) any wilful conduct which is of such a nature as is likely to drive the woman to commit suicide or to cause grave injury or danger to life, limb or health (whether mental or physical) of the woman; or,
(b) harassment of the woman where such harassment is with a view to coercing her or any person related to her to meet any unlawful demand Daljit Singh Vs. The State & Anr.
for any property or valuable security or is on account of failure by her or any person related to her to meet such demand."

sentences.text: 10. As per the allegations levelled in the FIR, the complainant has stated that she got married to accused on 17.07.2013 and immediately after marriage, her in-laws started complaining about bringing less dowry in the marriage and started giving beatings to her.
She also stated that they used to behave bestially with her.
Accused Daljit used to throw her out of the room in the night after abusing her in filthy language and giving beatings to her.
There is an allegation of illicit relations between accused Daljit Singh and sister-in-law (devrani) of complainant.
It is further stated in the complaint that on 04.02.2021 her in-laws alongwith accused threw her out of the house in the clothes which she was wearing and she was not allowed to enter the house.

11. In State of Bihar Vs. Ramesh Singh [1978] 1 S.C.R. 287 the Hon'ble Supreme Court while making observation on the point of framing of charge has held as under:

sentences.text: The allegations levelled by the complainant in the complaint have been specifically perused.
In order to invoke Section 498A IPC, there has to be specific demand of dowry and of harassment and cruelty in pursuance thereof.

Not even a single date or occasion has been mentioned in the complaint on which dowry was allegedly demanded by accused Daljit Singh from the complainant or that of cruelty meted out to her when said demand was not fulfilled.
The allegations made in the complaint are general and unspecific.
The complaint is not substantiated by any previous complaint against the accused before filing of the complaint on the basis of which FIR in question was registered.
There is no other document/MLC on record in order to show that complainant was beaten up at any point of time by the accused for not fulfilling the demand of dowry.
The findings of the learned Trial Court that specific allegations regarding throwing her out on 04.02.2021 prima facie constitutes offence under Section 498A IPC is completely erroneous.
13. The ingredients of Section 498A IPC are lacking.
In the absence of specific and unambiguous allegations regarding the demand of dowry and harassment/cruently in pursuance thereof, no case under Section 498A IPC is made out against the accused.
14. In view of the discussion made hereinabove, the impugned order dated 06.05.2025 is hereby set aside.
Accordingly, accused Daljit Singh is discharged of the offence under Section 498A IPC.
